title: Level Up a Build: Starter to Legend
lead: Every big build in this book comes in Starter, Pro and Legend sizes. Watch one little house level up, one move at a time.

steps.title: Starter: a box with a roof
steps.text: Start simple: four walls, a door, some windows and a roof. It is quick to build, and it already looks like a home.

steps.title: Pro move: add depth
steps.text: Flat walls look like cardboard. Put Spruce Logs on the corners and Cobblestone along the bottom. Add Cobblestone Stairs around the outside. Now the walls step in and out.

steps.title: Pro move: a second roof
steps.text: Build a small roof over the front door, held up by two fence posts. Pave under it with Stone Bricks. Two roofs give your build a much more interesting shape.

steps.title: Legend move: details
steps.text: Open trapdoors make shutters. A closed trapdoor with a Flower Pot on top makes a flower box. Add a chimney and a little window up high.

steps.title: Legend move: lights and a garden
steps.text: Hang a lantern under the porch beam. Put lanterns on fence posts by the path. Plant flowers and bushes. Now it is a Legend build!

body: Starter builds are quick, and they look finished. Pro builds add depth and a better shape. Legend builds add details, lights and a garden.
You can level up any build this way, even one you made last year. Do one move at a time. Then step back and look.
Most of these moves cost only a few extra blocks. Logs, trapdoors and lanterns make a big difference.
tips: Choose 3 or 4 main blocks before you start. This house uses Birch Planks, Dark Oak Stairs, Spruce Logs and Cobblestone.
Look at your build from far away and from every side. Fix any side that still looks flat.
Flowers can only be planted on blocks like grass and dirt. In Bedrock, a Flower Pot can sit on a closed trapdoor. Open the trapdoor and the pot breaks.
challenge: Pick one of your old builds. Give it one move from each step: depth, a second roof, a detail and a light.
